instruction: I need to update the title on the first slide of my presentation. Could you open the LibreOffice Impress file on my Desktop and change the title text from 'Presentation Title' to 'Emily Dickinson: Life and Works'? Please save the file after making the change.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1)

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the title on slide 1 from 'Presentation Title' to 'Emily Dickinson: Life and Works'. Evaluator verifies the title text has been updated correctly.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical flaw in title shape detection logic: getter returns the first non-empty text shape rather than specifically identifying the title shape

The assumption that 'first text shape is usually the title' is unreliable - slides can have multiple text shapes (subtitle, body text, text boxes) and shape iteration order is not guaranteed to prioritize titles
Could produce false positives if a non-title text shape appears first in the shape collection (e.g., a manually added text box)
Could produce false negatives if the title is not the first text shape returned by the iterator
The python-pptx library provides proper title detection methods (checking placeholder type or shape roles) which are not being used
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use proper title detection: check if shape.is_placeholder and shape.placeholder_format.type == PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE (requires importing from pptx.enum.shapes)
Alternative: check shape.has_text_frame and look for title-specific properties like shape name or layout position
Add fallback logic: if no proper title placeholder is found, then use the first text shape with a warning
Consider checking slide.shapes.title property if available in python-pptx for direct title access
